ui.day1Title: Privacy on day 1 in a new clinic
ui.day1Link: These checks are part of the opening playbook.
ui.placeholder: Placeholder: to be set with the data protection officer
ui.incident: Incident: report to the authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach.

screen-lock.title: Screen lock and screen position
screen-lock.example: Reception screens face away from the waiting room and lock after 5 minutes.

cabinet.title: Locked network cabinet
cabinet.example: Only the clinic manager and IT have the key; access is noted.

guest.title: Guest Wi-Fi isolation
guest.example: A guest phone reaches the internet only, not the clinic network or other guests.

vlans.title: VLAN separation
vlans.example: Medical devices and card terminals sit in their own networks, cut off from the rest.

encryption.title: Encrypted disks
encryption.example: FileVault is enforced by the MDM; the recovery key is escrowed there.

no-local.title: No local patient data
no-local.example: Records live in the practice software and on the file server, never on the Mac.

disposal.title: Secure disposal
disposal.example: Printer and X-ray PC drives are wiped or shredded with a certificate; paper goes into locked bins.

vpn.title: VPN encryption
vpn.example: Every byte between clinic and HQ runs through an IPsec tunnel.

tls.title: TLS to cloud services
tls.example: Practice software and payment provider are reached over HTTPS only.

no-mail.title: No patient data by plain e-mail
no-mail.example: Findings go through the practice software's portal, not as attachments.

rbac.title: Role-based access
rbac.example: Reception sees appointments and invoices; only vets open medical images.

admin-accounts.title: Separate admin accounts
admin-accounts.example: IT works with a normal account and uses the admin account only on the jump host.

mfa.title: Multi-factor login
mfa.example: Admin and remote access need a second factor.

audit.title: Logging and audit trail
audit.example: Logins and admin actions are logged centrally and kept for a set time.

backups.title: Encrypted, immutable backups
backups.example: Nightly backup, encrypted, with an offsite copy that nobody can change.

patching.title: Patching
patching.example: Hosts and servers are updated monthly in a fixed maintenance window.

iam.title: IAM with least privilege
iam.example: Each person and service gets only the cloud roles it needs.

no-shared.title: No shared credentials
no-shared.example: Every admin has a personal account; shared passwords live only in the vault.

rotation.title: Key and secret rotation
rotation.example: API keys and certificates are rotated on a schedule and on staff changes.

eu.title: Data location in the EU
eu.example: Practice software and backups are hosted in EU regions only.

dpa.title: Data processing agreements
dpa.example: A signed agreement with every provider that processes personal data.

ropa.title: Record of processing activities
ropa.example: Every system with personal data is listed with purpose, data and retention.

retention.title: Deletion and retention concept
retention.example: What is kept how long, and who deletes it when the period ends.

lifecycle.title: On- and offboarding
lifecycle.example: Accounts are created from roles and disabled on the last working day.

incident.title: Incident process
incident.example: Assess, contain, document, and report to the authority within 72 hours.

vendor.title: Vendor remote support rules
vendor.example: Device vendors connect only through the jump host, on request and for a limited time.

day1.cabinet: Network cabinet locked, key with the clinic manager only.
day1.screens: Reception screens turned away from the waiting room, screen lock tested.
day1.guest: Guest Wi-Fi isolation tested with a phone.
day1.macs: Every Mac encrypted and enrolled, checked in the MDM report.
day1.rules: Team briefed: no patient data by e-mail, no USB sticks.
day1.ropa: New clinic added to the record of processing activities.
